translations.literal: When there was appointment as Commissioner with the Same Privileges as the Three Excellencies and the Grand Year was in hai, he indeed died as Grand Master of the Palace.
translations.idiomatic: When there was appointment as Commissioner with the Same Privileges as the Three Excellencies and the Grand Year was in hai, he indeed died as Grand Master of the Palace.

sentences.zh: 文集傳於世。

translations.literal: His collected writings circulated in the world.
translations.idiomatic: His collected writings circulated in the world.

sentences.zh: 子順字景玄，方雅有父風，位太尉從事中郎。

translations.literal: His son Shun, styled Jingxuan, was refined and elegant with his father's manner, and held the post of Attendant-in-Ordinary on the Grand Commandant's staff.
translations.idiomatic: His son Shun, styled Jingxuan, was refined and elegant with his father's manner and held Attendant-in-Ordinary on the Grand Commandant's staff.

sentences.zh: 升明末卒。

translations.literal: He died at the end of the Shengming era.
translations.idiomatic: He died at the end of the Shengming era.

sentences.zh: 弟約。

translations.literal: His younger brother was Yue.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother was Yue.

sentences.zh: 約字景撝，少尚宋孝武女安吉公主，拜駙馬都尉。

translations.literal: Yue, styled Jingyi, in youth married Emperor Xiaowu of Song's daughter Princess Anji and was appointed Commandant Escort.
translations.idiomatic: Yue, styled Jingyi, in youth married Emperor Xiaowu of Song's daughter Princess Anji and was appointed Commandant Escort.

sentences.zh: 仕齊，累遷太子中庶子、領屯騎校尉。

translations.literal: Serving Qi, he was repeatedly promoted to Junior Mentor and Colonel of the Household Guards of Resolute Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: Serving Qi, he rose to Junior Mentor and Colonel of the Household Guards of Resolute Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 永明八年八月合朔，約脫武冠解劍，於省眠至下鼓不起，為有司所奏，贖論。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the eighth year of Yongming, at the new moon conjunction, Yue removed his martial cap and unsheathed his sword, slept in the office until the evening drum without rising, was reported by the relevant office, and was sentenced to ransom.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of Yongming year 8, at the new moon conjunction, Yue removed his martial cap and unsheathed his sword, slept in the office until the evening drum without rising, was reported, and was sentenced to ransom.

sentences.zh: 出為宜都王冠軍長史、淮南太守，行府州事。

translations.literal: He went out as Senior Administrator to Prince Yidu, Champion General, and Grand Administrator of Huainan, acting as Governor of the princely fief and province.
translations.idiomatic: He went out as Senior Administrator to Prince Yidu, Champion General, and Grand Administrator of Huainan, acting Governor of the princely fief and province.

sentences.zh: 武帝謂曰：「今用卿為近蕃上佐，想副我所期。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu told him: "Now I use you as close frontier chief aide—I trust you will meet what I expect."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu told him: "Now I use you as close frontier chief aide—I trust you will meet what I expect."

sentences.zh: 」約曰：「南豫密邇京師，不化自理，臣亦何人，爝火不息。

translations.literal: " Yue said: "Southern Yu is close to the capital; if it is not governed of itself, what kind of man am I that the torch flame does not cease?"
translations.idiomatic: " Yue said: "Southern Yu is close to the capital; if it is not governed of itself, what kind of man am I that the torch flame does not cease?"

sentences.zh: 」時諸王行事，多相裁割，約居右任，主佐之間穆如也。

translations.literal: At the time princes' acting administrators mostly mutually trimmed each other's authority; Yue held the right appointment and between lord and aide there was harmony.
translations.idiomatic: Princes' acting administrators mostly trimmed each other's authority; Yue held the right appointment and lord and aide were harmonious.

sentences.zh: 遷司徒左長史。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Senior Administrator on the Minister of Works' left staff.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Senior Administrator on the Minister of Works' left staff.

sentences.zh: 齊明帝為錄尚書輔政，百僚脫屐到席，約躡屐不改。

translations.literal: When Emperor Ming of Qi was Recording Secretary assisting in government, the hundred officials removed their shoes to the mat; Yue tread his shoes unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Ming of Qi was Recording Secretary assisting in government, the hundred officials removed their shoes to the mat; Yue tread his shoes unchanged.

sentences.zh: 帝謂江祏曰：「蔡氏是禮度之門，故自可悅。

translations.literal: The Emperor told Jiang Shi: "The Cai house is a gate of ritual measure—therefore it is naturally pleasing."
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor told Jiang Shi: "The Cai house is a gate of ritual measure—therefore it is naturally pleasing."

sentences.zh: 」祏曰：「大將軍有揖客，復見於今。」

translations.literal: " Shi said: "The Grand General had guests who bowed—again seen today."
translations.idiomatic: " Shi said: "The Grand General had guests who bowed—again seen today."

sentences.zh: 約好飲酒，夷淡不與世雜。

translations.literal: Yue loved drinking wine; plain and detached, he did not mix with the world.
translations.idiomatic: Yue loved drinking wine; plain and detached, he did not mix with the world.

sentences.zh: 永元二年，卒于太子詹事，年四十四，贈太常。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yongyuan he died as Household Steward to the Heir Apparent, age forty-four; he was posthumously made Minister of Ceremonies.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongyuan year 2 he died as Household Steward to the Heir Apparent, age forty-four; he was posthumously made Minister of Ceremonies.

sentences.zh: 弟撙。

translations.literal: His younger brother was Zun.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother was Zun.

sentences.zh: 撙字景節，少方雅退默，與第四兄寅俱知名。

translations.literal: Zun, styled Jingjie, from youth was refined, elegant, retiring, and silent; with his fourth elder brother Yin he was alike renowned.
translations.idiomatic: Zun, styled Jingjie, from youth was refined, elegant, retiring, and silent; with his fourth elder brother Yin he was alike renowned.

sentences.zh: 仕齊位給事黃門侍郎。

translations.literal: Serving Qi he held the post of Attendant Gentleman of the Yellow Gate.
translations.idiomatic: Serving Qi he held Attendant Gentleman of the Yellow Gate.

sentences.zh: 丁母憂，廬於墓側。

translations.literal: When his mother died he mourned in a hut beside the tomb.
translations.idiomatic: When his mother died he mourned in a hut beside the tomb.

sentences.zh: 齊末多難，服闋，因居墓所。

translations.literal: At the end of Qi troubles were many; when mourning ended he therefore dwelt at the tomb site.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Qi troubles were many; when mourning ended he dwelt at the tomb site.

sentences.zh: 除太子中庶子、太尉長史，並不就。

translations.literal: He was appointed Junior Mentor and Senior Administrator to the Grand Commandant, and accepted neither.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Junior Mentor and Senior Administrator to the Grand Commandant, and accepted neither.

sentences.zh: 梁台建，為侍中，遷臨海太守。

translations.literal: When the Liang regime was established he became Palace Attendant and was transferred to Grand Administrator of Linhai.
translations.idiomatic: When the Liang regime was established he became Palace Attendant and was transferred to Grand Administrator of Linhai.

sentences.zh: 公事左遷太子中庶子，復為侍中，吳興太守。

translations.literal: For public affairs he was demoted to Junior Mentor, again became Palace Attendant, and Grand Administrator of Wuxing.
translations.idiomatic: For public affairs he was demoted to Junior Mentor, again became Palace Attendant and Grand Administrator of Wuxing.

sentences.zh: 初，撙在臨海，百姓楊元孫以婢采蘭貼與同里黃權，約生子，酬乳哺直。

translations.literal: Earlier when Zun was at Linhai, commoner Yang Yuansun posted a maid Cailan together with fellow villager Huang Quan; they agreed she would bear a child and pay nursing wages.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier when Zun was at Linhai, commoner Yang Yuansun posted maid Cailan with fellow villager Huang Quan; they agreed she would bear a child and pay nursing wages.

sentences.zh: 權死後，元孫就權妻吳贖婢母子五人，吳背約不還。

translations.literal: After Quan died, Yuansun went to Quan's wife Wu to redeem the maid and mother with five persons; Wu broke the agreement and would not return them.
translations.idiomatic: After Quan died, Yuansun went to Quan's wife Wu to redeem maid and mother with five persons; Wu broke the agreement and would not return them.

sentences.zh: 元孫訴，撙判還本主。

translations.literal: Yuansun sued; Zun judged and returned them to the original master.
translations.idiomatic: Yuansun sued; Zun judged and returned them to the original master.

sentences.zh: 吳能為巫，出入撙內，以金釧賂撙妾，遂改判與吳。

translations.literal: Wu could perform shamanism and entered and left within Zun's household; with gold bracelets she bribed Zun's concubine, and the judgment was changed to give them to Wu.
translations.idiomatic: Wu could perform shamanism and entered Zun's household; with gold bracelets she bribed Zun's concubine, and the judgment was changed to give them to Wu.

sentences.zh: 元孫撾登聞鼓訟之，為有司劾。

translations.literal: Yuansun beat the Palace Gate drum to sue; Zun was impeached by the relevant office.
translations.idiomatic: Yuansun beat the Palace Gate drum to sue; Zun was impeached by the relevant office.

sentences.zh: 時撙已去郡，雖不坐，而常以為恥。

translations.literal: At the time Zun had already left the command; though he was not punished, he constantly took it as shame.
translations.idiomatic: Zun had already left the command; though not punished, he constantly took it as shame.

sentences.zh: 口不言錢，及在吳興，不飲郡井，齋前自種白莧紫茄，以為常餌，詔褒其清。

translations.literal: He did not speak of money; when at Wuxing he did not drink from the command well; before his study he himself planted white amaranth and purple eggplant as regular fare; an edict praised his purity.
translations.idiomatic: He did not speak of money; at Wuxing he did not drink from the command well; before his study he planted white amaranth and purple eggplant as regular fare; an edict praised his purity.

sentences.zh: 加信武將軍。

translations.literal: He was added as General of Trustworthy Martiality.
translations.idiomatic: He was added as General of Trustworthy Martiality.

sentences.zh: 時帝將為昭明太子納妃，意在謝氏。

translations.literal: At the time the Emperor wished to take a consort for Crown Prince Zhaoming; his intent was on the Xie clan.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor wished to take a consort for Crown Prince Zhaoming; his intent was on the Xie clan.

sentences.zh: 袁昂曰：「當今貞素簡勝，唯有蔡撙。

translations.literal: Yuan Ang said: "Among those today who are chaste, plain, and surpass others, there is only Cai Zun."
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Ang said: "Among those today who are chaste, plain, and surpass others, there is only Cai Zun."

sentences.zh: 」乃遣吏部尚書徐勉詣之，停車三通不報。

translations.literal: Thereupon Director of the Ministry of Personnel Xu Mian was sent to visit him; he stopped his carriage three times without response.
translations.idiomatic: Director of the Ministry of Personnel Xu Mian was sent to visit him; he stopped his carriage three times without response.

sentences.zh: 勉笑曰：「當須我召也。

translations.literal: Mian laughed and said: "He must need me to summon him."
translations.idiomatic: Mian laughed: "He must need me to summon him."

sentences.zh: 」遂投刺乃入。

translations.literal: Thereupon he submitted his calling card and only then entered.
translations.idiomatic: He submitted his calling card and only then entered.

sentences.zh: 天監九年，宣城郡吏吳承伯挾祅道聚眾攻宣城，殺太守朱僧勇，轉寇吳興，吏人並請避之。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Tianjian, Clerk of Xuancheng Command Wu Chengbo, relying on heterodox ways, gathered a crowd to attack Xuancheng, killed Grand Administrator Zhu Sengyong, then raided Wuxing; clerks and people all asked to flee.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianjian year 9, Xuancheng clerk Wu Chengbo, relying on heterodox ways, gathered a crowd to attack Xuancheng, killed Grand Administrator Zhu Sengyong, then raided Wuxing; clerks and people all asked to flee.

sentences.zh: 撙堅守不動，命眾出戰，摧破斬承伯，餘党悉平。

translations.literal: Zun firmly held without moving, ordered the crowd to go out and fight, crushed and beheaded Chengbo, and the remaining party was entirely pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Zun held firm, ordered the crowd out to fight, crushed and beheaded Chengbo, and the remainder was pacified.

sentences.zh: 累遷吏部尚書，在選弘簡有名稱。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Director of the Ministry of Personnel; in selections he was broad and plain with a renowned reputation.
translations.idiomatic: He was repeatedly promoted to Director of the Ministry of Personnel; in selections he was broad and plain with a renowned reputation.

sentences.zh: 又為侍中，領秘書監。

translations.literal: He again became Palace Attendant and headed the Palace Library.
translations.idiomatic: He again became Palace Attendant and headed the Palace Library.

sentences.zh: 武帝嘗謂曰：「卿門舊尚有堪事者多少？

translations.literal: Emperor Wu once said to him: "In your gate, how many are there still fit for affairs?"
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu once asked: "In your gate, how many are still fit for affairs?"

sentences.zh: 」撙曰：「臣門客沈約、範岫各已被升擢，此外無人。

translations.literal: " Zun said: "My gate's retainers Shen Yue and Fan Xiu have each already been promoted; beyond them there is no one."
translations.idiomatic: " Zun said: "My retainers Shen Yue and Fan Xiu have each been promoted; beyond them there is no one."

sentences.zh: 」約時為太子少傅，岫為右衛將軍。

translations.literal: Yue was then Junior Tutor to the Heir Apparent; Xiu was General of the Right Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Yue was Junior Tutor to the Heir Apparent; Xiu was General of the Right Guard.

sentences.zh: 撙風骨鯁正，氣調英嶷，當朝無所屈讓。

translations.literal: Zun's bearing was stern and upright, his spirit lofty and commanding; in the present court he yielded to none.
translations.idiomatic: Zun's bearing was stern and upright, his spirit lofty; in court he yielded to none.

sentences.zh: 嘗奏用琅邪王筠為殿中郎，武帝嫌不取參掌通署，乃推白牒於香橙地下，曰：「卿殊不了事。

translations.literal: He once memorialized to appoint Langya Wang Yun as Attendant Within the Gates; the Emperor disliked his not taking part in joint administration and pushed the white dossier to the ground beneath the fragrant orange and said: "You truly do not understand affairs."
translations.idiomatic: He once memorialized to appoint Langya Wang Yun as Attendant Within the Gates; the Emperor disliked his not taking part in joint administration and pushed the white dossier beneath the fragrant orange: "You truly do not understand affairs."

sentences.zh: 」撙正色俯身拾牒起，曰：「臣謂舉爾所知，許允已有前事；

translations.literal: " Zun with a stern face bent, picked up the dossier and rose, saying: "Your servant considers recommending those one knows—Xu Yun already had a prior case;
translations.idiomatic: " Zun sternly bent, picked up the dossier and rose: "I consider recommending those one knows—Xu Yun already had a prior case;

sentences.zh: 既是所知而用，無煩參掌署名。

translations.literal: since it is one known and used, there is no need for joint administration to sign.
translations.idiomatic: since it is one known and used, there is no need for joint administration to sign.

sentences.zh: 臣撙少而仕宦，未嘗有不了事之目。

translations.literal: Your servant Zun from youth entered office and has never borne the reputation of not understanding affairs."
translations.idiomatic: I, Zun, from youth entered office and have never borne the reputation of not understanding affairs."

sentences.zh: 」因捧牒直出，便命駕而去，仍欲抗表自解。

translations.literal: " He thereupon held the dossier straight out and left, immediately ordered his carriage and departed, and still wished to memorialized in protest to resign.
translations.idiomatic: He held the dossier straight out and left, ordered his carriage and departed, and still wished to memorialized in protest to resign.

sentences.zh: 帝尋悔，取事為畫。

translations.literal: The Emperor soon regretted it and took the affair as a lesson.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor soon regretted it and took the affair as a lesson.

sentences.zh: 帝嘗設大臣餅，撙在坐。

translations.literal: The Emperor once set out cakes for the great ministers; Zun was seated.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor once set out cakes for the great ministers; Zun was seated.

sentences.zh: 帝頻呼姓名，撙竟不答，食餅如故。

translations.literal: The Emperor repeatedly called his personal name; Zun did not answer at all and ate cake as before.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor repeatedly called his personal name; Zun did not answer and ate cake as before.

sentences.zh: 帝覺其負氣，乃改喚蔡尚書，撙始放箸執笏曰：「爾。

translations.literal: The Emperor perceived his proud spirit and changed to calling Director Cai; Zun then set down his chopsticks, took his baton and said: "Yes."
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor perceived his proud spirit and changed to calling Director Cai; Zun then set down chopsticks, took his baton and said: "Yes."

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「卿向何聾，今何聰？

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "You were deaf before—why are you hearing now?"
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said: "You were deaf before—why hearing now?"

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「臣預為右戚，且職在納言，陛下不應以名垂喚。

translations.literal: " He answered: "Your servant is by precedent a senior imperial relative and my office is to remonstrate; Your Majesty should not call by personal name."
translations.idiomatic: " He answered: "I am by precedent a senior imperial relative and my office is to remonstrate; Your Majesty should not call by personal name."

sentences.zh: 」帝有慚色。

translations.literal: The Emperor showed a look of shame.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor looked ashamed.

sentences.zh: 性甚凝厲，善自居適。

translations.literal: By nature he was very stern and severe, good at keeping himself at ease.
translations.idiomatic: By nature he was very stern, good at keeping himself at ease.

sentences.zh: 女為昭明太子妃，自詹事以下咸來造謁，往往稱疾相聞，間遣之。

translations.literal: His daughter was consort to Crown Prince Zhaoming; from Household Steward downward all came to call; he often claimed illness in reply and occasionally sent someone.
translations.idiomatic: His daughter was consort to Crown Prince Zhaoming; from Household Steward downward all came to call; he often claimed illness and occasionally sent someone.

sentences.zh: 及其引進，但暄寒而已，此外無復餘言。

translations.literal: When he received them for audience, he spoke only of cold and heat—beyond that no further words.
translations.idiomatic: When he received them, he spoke only of cold and heat—beyond that no further words.

sentences.zh: 後為中書令，卒于吳郡太守，諡曰康子。

translations.literal: Later he became Director of the Secretariat and died as Grand Administrator of Wu Command; his posthumous title was Master Kang.
translations.idiomatic: He later became Director of the Secretariat and died as Grand Administrator of Wu Command; his posthumous title was Master Kang.

sentences.zh: 司空袁昂嘗謂諸賓曰：「自蔡侯卒，不復更見此人。

translations.literal: Minister of Works Yuan Ang once told the guests: "Since Lord Cai's death, I have not again seen such a man."
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Works Yuan Ang once told guests: "Since Lord Cai's death, I have not again seen such a man."

sentences.zh: 」其為名輩所知如此。

translations.literal: He was known by leading men of reputation like this.
translations.idiomatic: He was known by leading men of reputation like this.

sentences.zh: 子彥深，宣城內史。

translations.literal: His son Yanshen was Interior Administrator of Xuancheng.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yanshen was Interior Administrator of Xuancheng.

sentences.zh: 彥深弟彥高，給事黃門侍郎。

translations.literal: Yanshen's younger brother Yangao was Attendant Gentleman of the Yellow Gate.
translations.idiomatic: Yanshen's younger brother Yangao was Attendant Gentleman of the Yellow Gate.

sentences.zh: 彥高子凝。

translations.literal: Yangao's son was Ning.
translations.idiomatic: Yangao's son was Ning.

sentences.zh: 尋授吏部侍郎。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed Vice Director of the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was appointed Vice Director of the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 凝年位未高，而才地為時所重，常端坐西齋，自非素貴名流，罕所交接，趣時者多譏焉。

translations.literal: Though Ning's years and rank were not yet high, his talent and standing were esteemed by the age; he constantly sat upright in the western study; except for old nobles and famous figures he rarely received visitors—those chasing the times mostly ridiculed him.
translations.idiomatic: Though Ning's years and rank were not yet high, his talent and standing were esteemed; he constantly sat upright in the western study; except for old nobles and famous figures he rarely received visitors—those chasing the times mostly ridiculed him.

sentences.zh: 宣帝嘗謂凝曰：「我欲用義興主婿錢肅為黃門侍郎，卿意如何？

translations.literal: Emperor Xuan once said to Ning: "I wish to use Princess Yixing's son-in-law Qian Su as Attendant of the Yellow Gate—what is your view?"
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuan once asked Ning: "I wish to use Princess Yixing's son-in-law Qian Su as Attendant of the Yellow Gate—what is your view?"

sentences.zh: 」凝正色曰：「帝鄉舊戚，恩由聖旨，則無所復問。

translations.literal: " Ning with a stern face said: "Imperial township old kin—the favor comes from the sage intent, then there is nothing further to ask.
translations.idiomatic: " Ning said sternly: "Imperial township old kin—if favor comes from the sage intent, there is nothing further to ask.

sentences.zh: 若格以僉議，黃散之職，故須人門兼美。

translations.literal: If measured by collective deliberation, the office of Attendant and Regular Attendant requires a gate with combined excellence."
translations.idiomatic: If measured by collective deliberation, Attendant and Regular Attendant requires a gate with combined excellence."

sentences.zh: 」帝默然而止。

translations.literal: The Emperor fell silent and stopped.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor fell silent and stopped.

sentences.zh: 肅聞而不平，義興公主日譖之，尋免官，遷交趾。

translations.literal: Su heard and was not at peace; Princess Yixing daily slandered him; soon he was removed from office and transferred to Jiaozhi.
translations.idiomatic: Su heard and was not at peace; Princess Yixing daily slandered him; soon he was removed and transferred to Jiaozhi.

sentences.zh: 頃之追還。

translations.literal: Before long he was recalled.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was recalled.

sentences.zh: 後主嗣位，為給事黃門侍郎。

translations.literal: When the Later Lord succeeded, he became Attendant Gentleman of the Yellow Gate.
translations.idiomatic: When the Later Lord succeeded, he became Attendant Gentleman of the Yellow Gate.

sentences.zh: 後主嘗置酒，歡甚，將移宴弘范宮，眾人咸從，唯凝與袁憲不行。

translations.literal: The Later Lord once set out wine, merriment very deep, and wished to move the feast to Hongfan Palace; the crowd all followed—only Ning and Yuan Xian did not go.
translations.idiomatic: The Later Lord once set out wine with deep merriment and wished to move the feast to Hongfan Palace; the crowd all followed—only Ning and Yuan Xian did not go.

sentences.zh: 後主曰：「何為？

translations.literal: The Later Lord said: "Why?"
translations.idiomatic: The Later Lord said: "Why?"

sentences.zh: 」凝曰：「長樂尊嚴，非酒後所過，臣不敢奉詔。

translations.literal: " Ning said: "Changle's dignity is not a place to pass through after wine—your servant dare not receive the order."
translations.idiomatic: " Ning said: "Changle's dignity is not a place to pass through after wine—I dare not receive the order."

sentences.zh: 」眾人失色。

translations.literal: The crowd changed color.
translations.idiomatic: The crowd changed color.

sentences.zh: 後主曰：「卿醉矣。

translations.literal: The Later Lord said: "You are drunk."
translations.idiomatic: The Later Lord said: "You are drunk."

sentences.zh: 」令引出。

translations.literal: He ordered him led out.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered him led out.

sentences.zh: 他日，後主謂吏部尚書蔡征曰：「蔡凝負地矜才，無所用也。

translations.literal: Another day the Later Lord told Director of the Ministry of Personnel Cai Zheng: "Cai Ning prides himself on standing and talent and is of no use."
translations.idiomatic: Another day the Later Lord told Director Cai Zheng: "Cai Ning prides himself on standing and talent and is of no use."

sentences.zh: 」尋遷信威晉熙王府長史，鬱鬱不得志。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to Senior Administrator to Prince Jinxi of Trustworthy Martiality; depressed, he did not achieve his intent.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was transferred to Senior Administrator to Prince Jinxi of Trustworthy Martiality; depressed, he did not achieve his intent.

sentences.zh: 乃喟然歎曰：「天道有廢興，夫子雲'樂天知命'，斯理庶幾可達。

translations.literal: He thereupon sighed and said: "Heaven's Way has decline and rise; the Master said 'rejoice in Heaven and know fate'—this principle can perhaps be reached."
translations.idiomatic: He sighed: "Heaven's Way has decline and rise; the Master said 'rejoice in Heaven and know fate'—this principle can perhaps be reached."

sentences.zh: 」因著小室賦以見志。

translations.literal: He therefore composed the "Small Chamber Rhapsody" to show his intent.
translations.idiomatic: He composed the "Small Chamber Rhapsody" to show his intent.

sentences.zh: 陳亡入隋，道病卒，年四十七。

translations.literal: When Chen fell and he entered Sui, he died on the road, age forty-seven.
translations.idiomatic: When Chen fell and he entered Sui, he died on the road, age forty-seven.

sentences.zh: 子君知，頗知名。

translations.literal: His son Junzhi was somewhat renowned.
translations.idiomatic: His son Junzhi was somewhat renowned.

sentences.zh: 論曰：蔡廓體業弘正，風格峻舉。

translations.literal: Commentary says: Cai Kuo's substance and career were broad and upright, his style lofty and rising.
translations.idiomatic: Commentary says: Cai Kuo's substance and career were broad and upright, his style lofty and rising.

sentences.zh: 興宗出內所踐，不隕家聲。

translations.literal: Xingzong in going out and entering what he tread did not fall from the family's reputation.
translations.idiomatic: Xingzong in what he tread going out and entering did not fall from the family's reputation.

sentences.zh: 位在具臣，而情懷伊、霍，仁者有勇，驗在斯乎。

translations.literal: His rank was among full ministers, yet his heart held Yi and Huo; the benevolent have courage—the proof is in this.
translations.idiomatic: His rank was among full ministers, yet his heart held Yi and Huo; the benevolent have courage—the proof is in this.

sentences.zh: 然自廓及凝，年移四代，高風素氣，無乏于時，其所以取貴，不徒然矣。

translations.literal: Yet from Kuo to Ning, years shifted through four generations; lofty wind and plain spirit did not fail in the age—the reason they won esteem was not for nothing.
translations.idiomatic: Yet from Kuo to Ning, years shifted through four generations; lofty wind and plain spirit did not fail in the age—the reason they won esteem was not for nothing.

sentences.zh: 至於矜倨之失，蓋其風俗所通，格以正道，故亦名教之深尤也。

translations.literal: As for the fault of haughty reserve—that is what their customs shared; measured by the upright Way, therefore it is also the deep fault of name and teaching.
